pr.title: Keep Codex hooks trusted across upgrades and resend timed-out submissions
pr.head: 065881738a3bc663ca33c75c68c76019bb090a41

summary: Projector's watch daemon delivers review and fix events to Codex sessions by running codex queue … --resume, and five Codex command hooks, each running project watch codex-hook, register the session and acknowledge each delivered batch. This pull request fixes two ways that delivery failed with nothing reporting it.

1. Every Projector release untrusted the hooks. Codex trusts a plugin's hooks by a hash of every file in the plugin, and the main projector plugin is the whole repository, so each release changed the hash and Codex stopped running the hooks. The hooks now ship as projector-hooks@projector, a plugin of their own in codex-hooks/ that a release leaves unchanged. watch add and watch status ask codex app-server whether Codex runs the hooks, and say how to fix it when it does not.
  2. A timed-out codex queue stranded its session. The daemon killed the call after 15 seconds and marked the batch uncertain, and nothing resent an uncertain batch unless someone ran project watch codex-retry. Because the daemon sends one batch per session at a time, every later event for that session waited. The call now gets 60 seconds, and an uncertain batch is resent 30 minutes after its submission unless the session's transcript shows it arrived.
Existing Codex users install the new plugin once, through install.sh or project upgrade, and trust its five hooks in /hooks.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Batch: the events the daemon sends a session in one codex queue call, stored under codex-pending/ until acknowledged.
  • Acknowledgment: the UserPromptSubmit hook seeing the batch's PROJECTOR WATCH <id> marker and writing a receipt.
  • Receipt: codex-receipts/<id>.json, which consumes a batch and blocks any later copy of it.
  • uncertain: a batch whose submission timed out or was interrupted, so nobody knows whether Codex accepted it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review, of afb5c69, opened two findings. Four commits answered them, and the review of 0658817 verified both fixed and found the head clean:

  • A daemon stopped during a codex queue call no longer waits for it, so it releases its lock within the 10-second stop wait.
  • The packaging test now checks that a simulated release leaves codex-hooks/ unchanged, instead of comparing versions, so a release to 1.0.0 no longer fails it.
  • Both suggestions were taken: listed_hooks closes its pipes, and the skill tables cover the events: none line about Codex hooks.

groups.title: Resending an uncertain submission
groups.kicker: The daemon now resends a timed-out batch on its own, 30 minutes after it was sent.
intro: When codex queue does not finish in time, the daemon cannot tell whether Codex accepted the message, so it marks the batch uncertain. The base never resent such a batch, and the session's later events waited behind it. Now _send records submitted_at, a timeout sets next_attempt_at to 30 minutes after it, and uncertain joins the states that prepare and _send send, SENDABLE.

Before a due resend, Dispatcher.tick still reads the transcript through confirm. A batch that appears there is consumed instead of resent. A copy that reaches Codex after the first was acknowledged finds the receipt and is blocked in UserPromptSubmit before it starts a turn. recover gives a submission the daemon died during the same 30-minute deadline.

When the daemon stops, Dispatcher.close no longer waits for a running codex queue call, so a replacement daemon can take over within its 10-second wait. The call keeps the session's submission lock, so the next daemon leaves that batch alone, and the old process records the call's result before it exits.

files.note: The resend states and deadline, and the new hook_problem and listed_hooks, which ask codex app-server for hooks/list.

checks.text: close returns without waiting for a running call. The submission lock is an flock that the next daemon's recover sees, so the batch stays submitting, and the interpreter joins the pool's thread before exit, which a standalone pool confirmed. With wait=True restored in a copy, test_close_leaves_a_running_submission_to_finish_and_record_its_result fails.
A timed-out batch goes to uncertain with its deadline at submitted_at plus RESEND, never to queued. The full suite passed at this head, including the resend and consume tests.
Run against Codex 0.169, listed_hooks returned the five project watch codex-hook hooks with camel-case eventName and trustStatus fields, and hook_problem returned None in about half a second.

files.note: Covers the resend at the deadline, an arrived batch consumed instead of resent, a close that leaves a running submission to finish, and hook_problem against a fake app-server, including one that never answers.

groups.title: Reporting hooks Codex does not run
groups.kicker: watch add and watch status say when Codex has stopped running Projector's hooks.
intro: While Codex runs none of the hooks, a new session never registers and a delivered batch is never acknowledged, yet watch add went on printing events: codex. codex_hook_problem in the CLI now asks Codex itself, through hook_problem, which applies Codex's own trust rules. It asks only for a session with a Codex registration, or one whose CODEX_SESSION_ID matches, so Claude Code sessions never start Codex.
watch add appends the problem and its fix to the events: line and returns it as codex_hooks with --json. watch status prints it as a codex hooks: line and a codex_hooks field.

checks.text: On a host with no codex, hook_problem returns None when Popen raises, and codex_hook_problem asks nothing when shutil.which finds no codex. Traced in the code at this head.

files.note: codex_hook_problem decides when to ask Codex, and watch_delivery and watch status print what it finds.
Runs watch add against a fake codex app-server for a registered session and for an unregistered Codex session.

groups.title: Shipping the hooks as their own plugin
groups.kicker: A release no longer changes the hooks plugin, so Codex keeps trusting it.
intro: Codex's marketplace served the projector plugin from the repository root, so its hooks shared a hash with every skill and document. The hooks now live in a projector-hooks plugin whose bundle is codex-hooks/: its own manifest at version 1.0.0 and the unchanged hooks.json. The release script bumps only the two root manifests, so this plugin's hash changes only when its hooks do.
The main Codex manifest no longer declares hooks, the marketplace lists the new plugin, and install.sh installs it after projector@projector.

files.note: The new plugin's manifest. Its version moves only when hooks.json changes.
Pins the plugin's contents and runs a release on a temporary copy to check that every file under codex-hooks/ stays the same.

checks.text: A copy of the release script whose set_version also rewrote the hooks manifest failed this comparison. The loop above it never releases the plugin's own version, so a release to 1.0.0 or past it passes.

files.note: Checks that install.sh codex installs the hooks plugin.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The living docs and the skills describe the resend, the new plugin, and the hook report.
intro: docs/cli.md describes the resend and the codex_hooks field, and docs/plugins.md adds the new plugin to the install and update commands. The implement, fix-pr, and review-pr skills tell an agent to pass a hook problem on to the user, and no longer ask for a decision before an uncertain batch is resent. The completed codex-delivery plan stays as its record.

files.note: Adds rows for the events: codex — but … and events: none — Codex is not running … lines, and the 30-minute resend.
Tells the agent to relay a hook problem, whether the line starts events: codex or events: none.
